text:
Kaitlan Collins stared Donald Trump down as he attacked her at the White House Correspondents' Dinner

Kaitlan Collins stared down President Donald Trump after he threw insults her way at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.

The president delivered his much-anticipated remarks at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, D.C. After starting off with a few jokes, he began a rambling speech targeting several of his enemies, including Collins, a reporter for CNN. Trump also appeared to doze off midway through the event, before his marathon speech.

Earlier in the night, Collins won the award for Excellence in Presidential News Coverage Under Deadline Pressure for her coverage of Trump. "I wanna personally congratulate CNN's Kaitlan Collins on receiving her award," said Trump. "It was all about me; it's a fake. She shouldn't get the award; it was a fake. But I didn't mind." It comes after a former Trump staffer revealed his 4 chilling predictions for what the president will do next.

The president called Collins a "young, attractive woman," but shamed her for not smiling at him. "I said, 'Kaitlan, you ever smile?' Smile! You have a nice position, you're at CNN fake news!"

Trump grimaced as he watched Collins accept her award earlier in the night. Collins won the broadcast category and received a $5,000 prize.

Trump slammed Collins for being a part of the "fake news" media

CNN colleague Wolf Blitzer presented the honor to Collins, commending her "depth of knowledge, access, and context" in covering Trump and the conflict in Ukraine. Collins took to the stage to claim her award, embracing Blitzer during the moment.

Prior to exiting the stage, Collins also moved toward President Trump to offer a handshake. While the president managed a smile, his facial expression appeared strained as she made her way to the stage.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt's lips appeared tight as she observed Collins heading toward the stage. Positioned between them, departing president of the White House Correspondents' Association, Weijia Jang, smiled and applauded for Collins.

Collins has clashed with Trump consistently throughout his second presidential term. She recently mocked the president while covering his Great American State Fair earlier this month, which drew disappointing attendance.

"For a president who often fixates on crowd size, so far the fair on Washington's National Mall hasn't exactly lived up to the hype," Collins said, positioned amid a thin crowd on the National Mall. Trump has also faced criticism for remarks he's directed at Collins, which have been characterized as "misogynistic" by his detractors.

Last month, Collins was targeted by the president in the Oval Office while responding to another reporter's question about his unsuccessful $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund proposal.

Trump rambled on during his speech (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A beautiful woman never smiles," Trump said of Collins, adding that she has "hatred in her eyes."

Trump added: "I never see a smile off her face. I see her standing there with hatred in her eyes, like she has hatred, because we had borders, because we have a strong military, because we cut our taxes, because we do things that everybody wanted, and then we win our election in a massive landslide."

The president launched into Collins again when she raised Republicans' concerns that the fund, which opponents labeled a "slush fund," could compensate January 6 rioters who served prison time for assaulting police officers. "The fake news, like CNN, like The New York Times, and like others, have abused our people, have abused our people so badly," said Trump.

"And you should be ashamed of yourself. You used to be a conservative. She was a conservative from Alabama, can you believe it? But CNN, in particular, does such false reporting, but now they have new ownership, so maybe it'll straighten out, but I doubt it."

This marked the second attempt at holding the event after a gunman opened fire at the Washington Hilton Hotel in April, prompting law enforcement agents to rush to the president's protection. Cole Tomas Allen is accused of breaching a Secret Service security checkpoint while carrying firearms and knives.

A law enforcement officer was hit in their bulletproof vest during the exchange of gunfire with Allen before he was eventually subdued.
